assessments.skill: Prove the entry skills in a small lab
assessments.experiment: Demonstrate each entry skill with a small owned fixture or permitted training environment. Record the actual setup, one observation per skill and any prerequisite you need to repair.
assessments.variant: Change a relevant identity, input or environment setting and predict the effect before repeating the demonstration.
assessments.control: Include a deliberately unmet prerequisite and distinguish setup failure from a result about the subject.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the environment and entry assumptions without following the setup notes.

assessments.skill: What authorizes this test?
assessments.experiment: Write rules of engagement for a loopback training app, including allowed actions, rate limits, stop conditions, contacts and evidence handling.
assessments.variant: Add a third-party login dependency and decide which requests must remain excluded until permission changes.
assessments.control: Show a technically reachable endpoint that the written scope forbids, and leave it untouched.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the difference between technical access, ownership and authorization.

assessments.skill: Follow a hypothesis, not a tool list
assessments.experiment: Inventory the disposable app, rank two vulnerability hypotheses, and run a small non-destructive check for each with sanitized request/response evidence.
assessments.variant: Move the app to a new port or change a visible header and revise the hypotheses using actual behavior.
assessments.control: Compare a real route with an intentionally nonexistent route so a generic error page is not counted as a finding.
assessments.recall: Given a new banner, name the next observation that could disprove your hypothesis.

assessments.skill: Two accounts, one boundary
assessments.experiment: In an explicitly designated authorization lesson, test an owner and a second account against the same synthetic object and explain the server-side boundary.
assessments.variant: Change the object or HTTP method and predict whether the authorization decision should change.
assessments.control: Demonstrate legitimate owner access and a denied unauthorized request on a corrected local equivalent.
assessments.recall: Explain why hiding a button is different from enforcing authorization.

assessments.skill: Who is this process allowed to be?
assessments.experiment: Create two local test roles or use a supplied permissions fixture, identify an overbroad grant, and repair it while recording before/after effective access.
assessments.variant: Change group membership or parent-directory permissions and predict the new access result.
assessments.control: Keep the intended reader working and demonstrate that the unrelated role remains denied.
assessments.recall: Explain the difference between authentication, authorization and process privilege.

assessments.skill: Make a finding another person can verify
assessments.experiment: Write one lab finding with exact target/version, minimal steps, sanitized evidence, severity rationale and a tested local repair.
assessments.variant: Give a peer a changed input or repeat on a second clean fixture and identify assumptions missing from the report.
assessments.control: Show that the fix rejects the bad case without breaking an ordinary valid request.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct a finding from its root cause without copying the original prose.

assessments.skill: Run a small authorized assessment
assessments.experiment: Perform scope confirmation, inventory, two hypothesis tests and one reproducible finding or justified negative result; deliver an executive summary and technical evidence.
assessments.variant: Change an account role or route and independently reassess whether the suspected weakness remains.
assessments.control: Include an out-of-scope action you deliberately excluded and a benign workflow that survives the repair.
assessments.recall: Explain the assessment chain, one false lead and what evidence changed your mind.

assessments.skill: Revisit the skill on a fresh problem
assessments.experiment: After a delay, attempt the fresh task and produce a reproducible evidence packet. Ask a peer to select or inspect the variation when possible; record assistance, failed hypotheses and remaining limits.
assessments.variant: Change a mechanism-relevant condition, rather than only resetting the old environment, and independently predict and test the resulting behavior.
assessments.control: Include a contrasting case where the mechanism should not apply and a legitimate operation that should remain valid.
assessments.recall: Explain what transferred, what required help and which prerequisite needs another small experiment.

assessments.skill: Measure an objective, not a shell
assessments.experiment: Author an engagement plan with rules of engagement, white-cell contacts, allowed assets, deconfliction, stop conditions and a defender measurement plan.
assessments.variant: Add an operational constraint such as unavailable endpoint logging and redesign the objective or telemetry plan honestly.
assessments.control: Show a scenario that appears successful technically but fails the stated business objective.
assessments.recall: State the difference between a penetration-test finding and an adversary-emulation objective.

assessments.skill: Choose techniques from evidence
assessments.experiment: Build a small ATT&CK-aligned hypothesis from a cited threat report, specifying prerequisites, observable effects and a harmless substitute for each risky action.
assessments.variant: Replace the assumed identity or endpoint type and remove techniques whose prerequisites no longer hold.
assessments.control: Include one plausible but unsupported technique and explain why it was excluded.
assessments.recall: Rebuild the evidence-to-technique chain and name its uncertainty.

assessments.skill: Know what the defender can see
assessments.experiment: Build a timeline joining the marker, account, process and network observations; label each missing source rather than inventing coverage.
assessments.variant: Change the marker path or process argument and predict which detection features remain stable.
assessments.control: Repeat an ordinary administration action and distinguish its evidence from the staged behavior.
assessments.recall: Explain which sensor would be needed to resolve a missing observation.

assessments.skill: Make a small emulation reversible
assessments.experiment: In a disposable authorized lab, run a reviewed marker-only micro-emulation, record setup and exact effects, then perform and verify cleanup.
assessments.variant: Change a nonessential filename or account context and predict whether the intended behavior is still observable.
assessments.control: Verify the artifact did not exist before, appears during the test, and is absent after cleanup; preserve unrelated files.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the prerequisites and rollback steps without running a script blindly.

assessments.skill: Test detection with a partner
assessments.experiment: Have a defender or second review pass classify shuffled benign and emulated events; record misses, false positives and one revised analytic.
assessments.variant: Change a superficial indicator while preserving behavior and retest the revised analytic.
assessments.control: Include an administration lookalike that should remain unalerted or receive a documented lower-confidence classification.
assessments.recall: Explain why a detection that matches only the demonstration filename is fragile.

assessments.skill: Deliver a defensible exercise report
assessments.experiment: Run the scoped sequence in a resettable lab, measure defender visibility and response, and deliver an objective-based report with technical evidence and remediation retests.
assessments.variant: Withhold one assumed permission or telemetry source and adapt the plan without exceeding scope.
assessments.control: Demonstrate reset to baseline and distinguish untested coverage from a demonstrated miss.
assessments.recall: Explain what the exercise supports about defensive readiness and what it cannot establish.

assessments.skill: Turn an alert into a question
assessments.experiment: Triage a synthetic queue containing a login anomaly, a web alert and a harmless maintenance event; assign urgency using evidence and business context.
assessments.variant: Change an asset from a sandbox to a critical service and justify whether prioritization changes.
assessments.control: Keep a noisy but low-impact event from outranking a corroborated compromise solely because of event volume.
assessments.recall: Explain event, alert, incident, severity and confidence using one example.

assessments.skill: Follow the entity across logs
assessments.experiment: Build reproducible queries over a supplied dataset to trace an identity, host and source address through a bounded time window, recording missing fields.
assessments.variant: Change the time zone or host identifier in a synthetic copy and adjust the query without losing the same activity.
assessments.control: Include a similarly named account and an event outside the window that must not be joined.
assessments.recall: Recreate the query logic from the investigation question rather than memorizing syntax.

assessments.skill: Investigate a suspicious sign-in
assessments.experiment: Investigate a provided authentication timeline, rank account misuse against benign alternatives, and identify the next discriminating evidence.
assessments.variant: Add a service-account explanation or a contradictory device event and update the conclusion.
assessments.control: Include known maintenance logins and avoid treating location or failure count alone as compromise.
assessments.recall: Explain which evidence would raise or lower confidence in account misuse.

assessments.skill: Preserve evidence before following a lure
assessments.experiment: Correlate an inert phishing-style message fixture with proxy/DNS and application logs, recording user exposure separately from demonstrated execution.
assessments.variant: Change a redirect or add a blocked request and reassess how far the activity progressed.
assessments.control: Include a legitimate message with similar wording and a blocked attempt with no evidence of execution.
assessments.recall: Explain why receipt, click, execution and compromise are separate claims.

assessments.skill: Make containment proportionate
assessments.experiment: Write and rehearse a lab incident runbook that preserves evidence, escalates uncertainty, contains a synthetic account or endpoint, and verifies intended access afterward.
assessments.variant: Make the affected system unavailable to the responder and choose an alternative action with explicit residual risk.
assessments.control: Show that an unrelated account or service still works after containment.
assessments.recall: State the evidence needed before choosing a disruptive action.

assessments.skill: Close the case so someone can reopen it
assessments.experiment: Investigate an unfamiliar small log bundle and deliver a timeline, evidence references, confidence, response decision and shift handoff with unresolved questions.
assessments.variant: Add a late contradictory event and revise the disposition while retaining the earlier reasoning.
assessments.control: Document one rejected hypothesis and a known-benign comparison; do not turn missing logs into a clean bill of health.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the case and next action from the handoff alone after a delay.

assessments.skill: Draw the domain before testing it
assessments.experiment: On a training domain, document DNS discovery, one domain join and a normal domain sign-in; preserve an architecture diagram and baseline event evidence.
assessments.variant: Change the client DNS server in the disposable lab and predict which discovery or authentication step fails.
assessments.control: Compare a local login with a domain login and explain which identity authority answered.
assessments.recall: Recreate the domain discovery and trust boundaries from memory.

assessments.skill: A ticket is not a password
assessments.experiment: Capture permitted authentication telemetry in a training domain and correlate ticket issuance or fallback with a controlled client action, without collecting real credentials.
assessments.variant: Change a service name or introduce documented clock skew in the disposable lab and predict the failure or fallback.
assessments.control: Include a normal successful service access and a deliberately invalid service reference.
assessments.recall: Explain why DNS, SPNs and time synchronization matter to Kerberos.

assessments.skill: Prove an identity graph edge
assessments.experiment: Trace a least-privilege violation in a supplied or owned directory graph and verify the claimed edge against native permissions before proposing a fix.
assessments.variant: Remove one group membership or inherited permission and predict whether the path still exists.
assessments.control: Include a graph edge that appears plausible but is denied by the effective permissions.
assessments.recall: Explain the distinction between a graph hypothesis and a verified authorization path.

assessments.skill: Separate management power from service identity
assessments.experiment: Inspect a training GPO and a documented delegation configuration, explain their intended function and identify an overbroad grant using effective access and normal service behavior.
assessments.variant: Restrict the policy link or delegated target and predict which administrative or service action stops working.
assessments.control: Keep an intended management action functioning after the proposed least-privilege change.
assessments.recall: Explain why controlling a policy object and applying that policy are separate conditions.

assessments.skill: Follow the certificate enrollment decision
assessments.experiment: In an isolated AD CS lab or supplied configuration exercise, map template enrollment permissions and identity settings to a concrete authentication risk; test a corrected configuration in a real lab before claiming operational completion.
assessments.variant: Change enrollment rights or an identity-related template setting and predict which request is permitted or rejected.
assessments.control: Show a legitimate enrollment still works and an unauthorized identity request is rejected after the repair.
assessments.recall: Explain why possessing a valid certificate is not sufficient proof of an authorized identity.

assessments.skill: Harden a small domain and retest it
assessments.experiment: Audit the training domain's discovery, authentication, permissions and one certificate or policy boundary; deliver native evidence, impact and a verified least-privilege repair.
assessments.variant: Change one account's memberships or a policy scope and independently re-evaluate the affected path.
assessments.control: Retest normal user/service sign-in and document which enterprise controls were not present in the lab.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct one privilege path and the exact permission change that removed it.

assessments.skill: Identify who owns each control
assessments.experiment: Build an asset and responsibility inventory covering account ownership, regions, exposed endpoints, audit sources and recovery responsibilities.
assessments.variant: Move one component from a VM to a managed service and revise the shared-responsibility assumptions.
assessments.control: Include a provider-managed control that a workload operator cannot fix by changing application code.
assessments.recall: Explain the difference between provider security and secure use of the provider.

assessments.skill: Predict the authorization decision
assessments.experiment: Build an access matrix for two synthetic roles and one resource, test it in a provider policy simulator or scoped training account, and record where the simulator lacks runtime context.
assessments.variant: Add a condition or a resource policy and predict how the effective decision changes.
assessments.control: Demonstrate a denied unrelated principal and an intended allowed operation.
assessments.recall: Explain why an identity policy alone may not determine effective access.

assessments.skill: Public does not always mean intended
assessments.experiment: Trace a fictional application's exposure through load balancer, workload and data storage; validate selected rules using a local model or training account and propose a minimal repair.
assessments.variant: Change a resource from private to shared-with-one-role and verify that the intended boundary survives.
assessments.control: Preserve legitimate client access and demonstrate that an unrelated identity cannot read the object.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the layers required to explain one exposure finding.

assessments.skill: Separate workload identity from static keys
assessments.experiment: Replace a toy long-lived credential with a bounded local token or a training-provider workload identity, test expiration/revocation and document remaining trust assumptions.
assessments.variant: Change the audience, role or expiry and predict whether the request should still authenticate.
assessments.control: Verify a valid authorized request succeeds and a stale token is rejected without logging its contents.
assessments.recall: Explain rotation, revocation and short-lived identity as different mechanisms.

assessments.skill: Follow a control-plane change
assessments.experiment: Investigate supplied cloud audit events around a permission change and later resource access; construct a timeline and a detection query with explicit missing sources.
assessments.variant: Change a resource name or actor and test whether the behavioral analytic still finds the sequence.
assessments.control: Include a denied change and a known maintenance change that must not be labeled successful compromise.
assessments.recall: Explain what the audit source can and cannot establish about data access.

assessments.variant: Change one trust policy or network boundary and independently reassess the affected access path.
assessments.control: Verify legitimate workload behavior and prove temporary lab resources were removed where a real account was used.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the finding, provider-specific limits and remaining assurance gaps.

assessments.skill: A container still shares a kernel
assessments.experiment: Run a toy service with a non-root user, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges and a read-only root plus a bounded writable directory; explain observed failures.
assessments.variant: Remove one required write path or change its owner and predict which operation fails.
assessments.control: Preserve the service's intended request while showing it cannot write to an unrelated path.
assessments.recall: Explain which risks these controls reduce and which require stronger isolation.

assessments.skill: Know exactly which image ran
assessments.experiment: Generate an image inventory/SBOM for a toy service, pin the source image digest and record provenance, vulnerability findings and applicability limits.
assessments.variant: Resolve an updated tag and identify the changed digest and dependencies before accepting it.
assessments.control: Include a scanner finding for an unused or unreachable component and separate presence from demonstrated exploitability.
assessments.recall: Explain why a matching digest gives identity but not a guarantee of safety.

assessments.skill: Test an isolation claim
assessments.experiment: In a disposable project, verify loopback-only access, separate lab networks, resource bounds and the absence of tracker-volume or Docker-socket mounts.
assessments.variant: Move the client to another lab network and predict which target it should fail to reach.
assessments.control: Confirm a permitted same-network request works while cross-network and outbound probes fail within bounded timeouts.
assessments.recall: Explain what an internal bridge blocks and why the host kernel is still shared.

assessments.skill: Give the workload only its job
assessments.experiment: In a disposable Kubernetes cluster, bind a limited service account to one namespace and verify allowed and denied operations with the API authorization checks.
assessments.variant: Change the namespace or requested verb and predict the decision before checking.
assessments.control: Keep the intended read working and deny writes to unrelated secrets or namespaces.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the subject, role and binding needed for one API permission.

assessments.skill: Observe enforcement, not just YAML
assessments.experiment: Deploy a tiny client/server pair on an isolated test cluster, apply default-deny plus a specific allow rule, and test actual connectivity.
assessments.variant: Change one pod label or allowed port and predict which connection changes.
assessments.control: Include a matching permitted client and an unmatched client that must be denied; report an unsupported CNI as an unmet prerequisite.
assessments.recall: Explain why a valid NetworkPolicy object can coexist with unrestricted traffic.

assessments.skill: Review and repair a workload deployment
assessments.experiment: Review a fresh toy deployment, demonstrate one excessive permission or exposure, apply a minimal fix and retest the intended workload plus resource limits.
assessments.variant: Change a namespace, image version or writable path and revise the controls instead of copying the old manifest.
assessments.control: Show an unrelated workload and legitimate client remain functional after the fix.
assessments.recall: Explain one runtime observation that would invalidate your review conclusion.

assessments.experiment: Build a threat model with three concrete abuse cases and map each to an ASVS-style testable requirement.
assessments.variant: Add a background worker or third-party integration and revise the boundaries and threats.
assessments.control: Include a failure outside the service's responsibility and document the dependency instead of claiming to fix it.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct one threat from asset through entry point to consequence.

assessments.skill: Follow untrusted data to its sink
assessments.experiment: Repair one input or output handling defect in your own code and write tests that reproduce the defect and preserve intended behavior.
assessments.variant: Change the input encoding or rendering context and update the defense rather than reusing an unrelated escaping rule.
assessments.control: Include valid punctuation and an invalid structured input; reject the dangerous case without silently corrupting legitimate data.
assessments.recall: Explain why validation and output encoding address different boundaries.

assessments.skill: Put authorization beside the resource
assessments.experiment: Implement server-side authorization tests for owner access, cross-user access and the privileged operation; demonstrate the bug before the repair.
assessments.variant: Add a new HTTP method or background operation and check that it enforces the same resource policy.
assessments.control: Keep owner access working and deny an authenticated but unauthorized user.
assessments.recall: State the policy independently of route names or UI controls.

assessments.skill: Make a dependency decision you can defend
assessments.experiment: Produce an SBOM and pinned dependency manifest, investigate one advisory's applicability, and test an update or documented mitigation.
assessments.variant: Introduce a version change in a branch and assess both security and compatibility effects before merging.
assessments.control: Include an advisory that does not apply to the used component/version and explain the evidence.
assessments.recall: Explain why dependency presence, reachability and exploitability are separate claims.

assessments.skill: Make the pipeline stop for a real defect

assessments.variant: Change a fixture's filename or encoding and test whether the intended check still applies.
assessments.control: Confirm clean code builds successfully and no test prints secret-like fixture values into published logs.
assessments.recall: Explain the failure mode each gate detects and one it misses.

assessments.experiment: Deliver the toy service with passing regression tests, reproducible build inputs, deployment permissions, rollback instructions and a documented residual risk.
assessments.variant: Change a dependency or deployment setting and rerun only the checks whose assumptions changed, explaining the choice.
assessments.control: Reproduce a known security regression on the old version and show the release rejects it while valid use works.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the assurance argument and the strongest remaining limitation.

assessments.skill: Keep the original evidence original
assessments.experiment: Create an evidence manifest with acquisition time, source, hashes, handling history and analysis-copy paths; verify the original remains unchanged after analysis.
assessments.variant: Change the copy or filename and determine which identity assertions still hold.
assessments.control: Include a corrupted copy that must fail integrity verification and a byte-identical renamed copy that must pass content verification.
assessments.recall: Explain integrity, provenance and chain of custody as different properties.

assessments.skill: Recover a story from file metadata
assessments.experiment: Build a bounded account of file creation/modification using an analysis copy, recording filesystem semantics and tool/version assumptions.
assessments.variant: Change the timezone display or introduce a copied file whose timestamps differ from its real acquisition time.
assessments.control: Include metadata that cannot prove who created a file and explicitly withhold that conclusion.
assessments.recall: Explain why one timestamp does not prove an event happened at that exact time.

assessments.skill: Reconcile clocks before drawing conclusions
assessments.experiment: Correlate a small authentication, process and network evidence bundle into a timeline with confidence and source references.
assessments.variant: Add a clock-skew correction or delayed event and revise the ordering where justified.
assessments.control: Keep an unrelated similarly named process out of the incident chain.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct which event ordering is certain and which depends on clock assumptions.

assessments.skill: Separate a process artifact from a verdict
assessments.experiment: On a suitable analysis host, inspect process and connection artifacts from a public training image, compare them with the provided ground truth where available, and record unsupported interpretations.
assessments.variant: Change the filter or investigate a second process and independently test the same hypothesis.
assessments.control: Include a benign process with a suspicious-looking name and avoid treating its name alone as malware proof.
assessments.recall: Explain how an incompatible symbol profile can invalidate an apparently plausible result.

assessments.skill: Preserve the question while containing the risk
assessments.experiment: Rehearse a synthetic incident using a disposable service: preserve relevant logs, disable only the affected test identity and verify intended service behavior.
assessments.variant: Remove access to one evidence source and revise the plan without inventing missing facts.
assessments.control: Preserve a legitimate user's access and document evidence lost because of the chosen intervention.
assessments.recall: Explain one containment tradeoff and how it changes later interpretation.

assessments.variant: Introduce one contradictory artifact and revise the explanation while retaining an audit of the earlier hypothesis.
assessments.control: Identify one tempting conclusion that the available evidence does not support.

assessments.skill: Is the advisory actually applicable?
assessments.experiment: Validate a supplied finding against exact component/configuration evidence and classify confirmed, not applicable or insufficient evidence.
assessments.variant: Change a required feature or version and revise applicability.
assessments.control: Include a matching product name with a nonaffected version.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the conditions required before calling the finding applicable.

assessments.skill: Prioritize action using context
assessments.experiment: Prioritize a synthetic queue using exposure, business impact, exploitation evidence and an explicit SSVC-style decision path.
assessments.variant: Change exposure or exploitation evidence and justify the revised action.
assessments.control: Include a high-score isolated lab finding and a lower-score exposed critical asset.
assessments.recall: Explain which new evidence would change the highest priority.

assessments.skill: Verify the repair rather than the ticket
assessments.experiment: Apply a patch or configuration mitigation in an owned test service and verify both the vulnerable condition and normal functionality.
assessments.variant: Change the deployment variant and reassess whether the same mitigation applies.
assessments.control: Keep a ticket marked resolved from passing when the affected instance still has the old configuration.
assessments.recall: Explain patch presence versus effective remediation.

assessments.skill: Put an expiry date on accepted risk
assessments.experiment: Write a bounded exception for a fictional unpatchable service, with measurable compensating controls and a retest trigger.
assessments.variant: Remove a compensating control or change external exposure and reevaluate the exception.
assessments.control: Reject an indefinite exception without an accountable owner.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct when the exception must return to the remediation queue.

assessments.skill: Measure reduction in exposure
assessments.experiment: Produce a vulnerability-management report from a synthetic inventory, separating verified fixes, accepted risk, missing data and recurring causes.
assessments.variant: Add previously unknown assets and revise the metrics without hiding the changed denominator.
assessments.control: Distinguish a fall in scan coverage from a real reduction in exposure.
assessments.recall: Explain one metric that could look better while security became worse.

assessments.skill: Revisit the skill on a fresh problem
assessments.experiment: After a delay, attempt the fresh task and produce a reproducible evidence packet. Ask a peer to select or inspect the variation when possible; record assistance, failed hypotheses and remaining limits.
assessments.variant: Change a mechanism-relevant condition, rather than only resetting the old environment, and independently predict and test the resulting behavior.
assessments.control: Include a contrasting case where the mechanism should not apply and a legitimate operation that should remain valid.
assessments.recall: Explain what transferred, what required help and which prerequisite needs another small experiment.

assessments.skill: Prove the entry skills in a small lab
assessments.experiment: Demonstrate each entry skill with a small owned fixture or permitted training environment. Record the actual setup, one observation per skill and any prerequisite you need to repair.
assessments.variant: Change a relevant identity, input or environment setting and predict the effect before repeating the demonstration.
assessments.control: Include a deliberately unmet prerequisite and distinguish setup failure from a result about the subject.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the environment and entry assumptions without following the setup notes.

assessments.skill: Treat program rules as part of the target
assessments.experiment: Build a research plan using only an owned training target and a clearly testable vulnerability hypothesis.
assessments.variant: Add an excluded third-party integration and revise the plan.
assessments.control: Identify a technically possible test that the scope disallows.
assessments.recall: Explain why a public bug-bounty page does not authorize every asset or technique.

assessments.skill: Find the invariant the software should preserve
assessments.experiment: Form a root-cause hypothesis from the code and design a minimal experiment that could disprove it.
assessments.variant: Change input encoding or operation order and predict the effect on the invariant.
assessments.control: Include a normal edge case that looks unusual but preserves the intended rule.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the vulnerability hypothesis without relying on a scanner label.

assessments.skill: Make a small test generator teach you something
assessments.experiment: Write a bounded local input generator or property-based test, reproduce one failure and minimize the triggering fixture.
assessments.variant: Change the parser or seed corpus and verify the failure still tests the same property.
assessments.control: Include malformed input that is correctly rejected and must not count as a vulnerability.
assessments.recall: Explain crash, bug, security impact and exploitability as separate claims.

assessments.skill: Prove only the minimum necessary effect
assessments.experiment: Demonstrate a harmless synthetic impact in an owned reproduction and document exactly which privileges and data were involved.
assessments.variant: Change the user role or object class and test whether the impact generalizes.
assessments.control: Include a failed unauthorized action and avoid claiming access merely from a different response size.
assessments.recall: Explain one stronger impact claim the evidence does not support.

assessments.skill: Write a report that survives first triage
assessments.experiment: Produce a private training report with minimal reproducer, sanitized evidence and a proposed tested fix; do not submit to third parties as part of this exercise.
assessments.variant: Have a peer or fresh environment follow the report with a changed fixture and repair any missing assumption.
assessments.control: Keep credentials and live user data out of the evidence packet.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the report's root cause in two precise sentences.

assessments.skill: Generalize the mechanism carefully
assessments.experiment: Test the hypothesis on the new component, report positive or negative evidence, and produce a regression test and bounded generalization.
assessments.variant: Change one relevant implementation detail and explain why the mechanism applies or fails.
assessments.control: Include a superficially similar implementation where the required condition is absent.
assessments.recall: Explain which properties transfer and which were accidents of the first target.

assessments.control: Include a contrasting case where the mechanism should not apply and a legitimate operation that should remain valid.

assessments.control: Include a deliberately unmet prerequisite and distinguish setup failure from a result about the subject.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the environment and entry assumptions without following the setup notes.

assessments.skill: Treat generated text as untrusted input
assessments.experiment: Build a threat model that identifies which component may authorize each action and where untrusted text enters.
assessments.variant: Add an external document source and revise the trust assumptions.
assessments.control: Reject the idea that a model's assertion of permission is an authorization decision.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the tool-action boundary without referring to the system prompt.

assessments.skill: Keep a document from becoming an instruction
assessments.experiment: In a deterministic toy pipeline, test adversarial documents and enforce authorization outside the mock model before any data access or action.
assessments.variant: Change the document wording or source label and verify the same application boundary still holds.
assessments.control: Keep a legitimate document answer working and deny a requested unrelated data access.
assessments.recall: Explain why prompt wording alone cannot enforce a data-access policy.

assessments.skill: Validate what the application will execute
assessments.experiment: Add strict schemas and safe handling to a toy assistant's output pipeline and test malformed or unauthorized synthetic outputs.
assessments.variant: Nest a field or change output encoding and predict whether validation rejects it.
assessments.control: Preserve a valid allowed output while rejecting an extra privileged field.
assessments.recall: Explain schema validity versus authorization of a valid action.

assessments.skill: Give an agent a bounded capability
assessments.experiment: Implement or test an allowlisted dispatcher with synthetic files and a mock model; verify that model output cannot expand the allowed resource set.
assessments.variant: Change a resource identifier or attempt a second action outside the allowlist.
assessments.control: Permit the intended action and reject traversal-like or unrelated resource references.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct where least privilege is enforced independently of the model.

assessments.skill: Test retrieval separation between users
assessments.experiment: Test retrieval filters and result handling in an owned fixture so one user's documents cannot be returned to another user.
assessments.variant: Change a document ID, cache key or role and independently retest isolation.
assessments.control: Include a shared public document that remains legitimately accessible to both users.
assessments.recall: Explain why hiding a private citation after retrieval is too late to guarantee isolation.

assessments.skill: State exactly what the evaluation measured
assessments.experiment: Run the cases against the toy system, record failures and repairs, and distinguish deterministic application tests from any real-model observations.
assessments.variant: Add an unseen wording or tool-output shape and rerun the relevant boundary checks.
assessments.control: Include benign lookalikes so blocking every input cannot pass the evaluation.
assessments.recall: Explain why a passing finite test set does not prove universal prompt-injection resistance.
